_comment: Copy this file to config/config.local.json and fill in the values, or let `python scripts/setup.py` write it for you. config.local.json is git-ignored and must never be committed.

setup._comment: How this machine is set up: 'company' (an IT-provided opencode.json points OpenCode at an internal gateway) or 'private' (OpenCode logs in to a provider account of your own). Written by the setup wizard.

storage._comment: Written by the setup wizard: the name of this machine, recorded in the audit trail.

runtime._comment: Where the audit trail and OpenCode debug output are written. Never cleared by any tool. Empty means no audit trail.

knowledge._comment: The board's knowledge source: a folder of Markdown notes, such as an Obsidian vault. Read for every question, written to only after you confirm a memory entry when closing a topic. token_budget is the default of the knowledge slider on the confirm screen: how many tokens of vault sections each member receives (ranked for the topic and for the member). Empty vault_path means the board answers from your question alone. project is the default of the project picker on the home page: one project name, or several separated by commas. Notes whose front matter lists projects: [...] are used only when they name one of them, notes without the property are common to all projects; empty means every note is used. kpi_stale_days is how old a KPI note may be before members are told to say so before relying on it. roles_folder is the one folder whose role profiles define the board's members (section 3.4): one file per role or one file with several roles; empty means Roles/ inside the vault, and the examples shipped under roles/ when that does not exist. Read on every run, never part of the ranked selection. selection is the default of the Knowledge selection dropdown on the confirm screen (section 5.1): ai lets the model pick, per member, from the Python candidates in one extra call; python uses the Python ranking alone, no extra call. vault_name is the Obsidian vault name the Ask the vault sources link to (obsidian://open); empty means the vault folder's name. contents_limit_tokens (section 5.3) is the most the table of contents may take in the choosing call; above it the pages the word ranking puts first for the question are kept and the picks screen says the list was trimmed. core_skip_headings (section 5.4) names the sections of the project page the shared core leaves out, matched by their start without regard to case; they stay in the table of contents and the outline. An empty list skips nothing.

server._comment: The browser interface listens on 127.0.0.1 only. site_name is the name the browser uses. A plain name becomes a name under .localhost (program-mind -> http://program-mind.localhost:<port>/): every name under .localhost resolves to this machine in Chrome, Edge and Firefox without admin rights. A name that already carries a dot is used as it stands (program-mind.local), but nothing here makes such a name resolve - that needs a hosts-file entry or an mDNS responder, and both need admin rights. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only either way. history_folder is where the work of every agent is kept, one JSON file per board topic and per Ask the vault thread, never in the vault; empty means history/ next to config.local.json. The older name threads_folder is still read.

ask._comment: Ask the vault (spec section 10): one agent answering any question from the vault. Since section 5.6 every question reads the whole vault, every page whole, in one call, as long as it fits knowledge.max_read_tokens (the ceiling of one read, which since section 5.8 governs the board too; the older ask.max_read_tokens below is still read). Only when the vault outgrows the ceiling does the model rank the pages first and a check after the answer swap in pages left unread, up to max_reads rounds. token_budget is kept on the record of older threads and caps nothing.

provider._comment: models.board is the provider/model string OpenCode expects, e.g. 'anthropic/claude-opus-5' for a private account, or whatever provider/model your company's opencode.json defines. endpoint is only a record of which endpoint was approved (AI-3); it is not read per call. token_limits.board null means no limit is observed. opencode.config_file points at a company-provided opencode.json (the file from IT that defines the provider and the gateway) and is passed as OPENCODE_CONFIG (OC-8); never this file - OpenCode rejects it with 'unrecognized keys'. Leave empty for a private setup. opencode.auto_approve adds --auto where the installed version has it (OC-6, OC-7). opencode.extra_args appends further arguments to every run, one string per argument, e.g. --agent plan (OC-9). opencode.mode (spec 4.1) picks how OpenCode is called: auto (the default - one 'opencode serve' beside the program, so the page can show the answer as the model writes it, falling back to a run per call when the server will not start), serve, or run. Only the server streams; everything else about a call is the same either way.
